01 / FRAME & RACK

A full-height storage cassette

Bolted frame, leveling feet, rear panel, 25 shelves, ten locator lanes, and 250 separate carriers. Removable front leaves expose the rack for service.

02 / MOTION

One carrier at a time

Upper and lower horizontal guides support the mast. The lift runs vertically; a third slide transfers the carrier between shelf, shuttle and dock.

03 / HANDOFF

A two-door transfer chamber

A captive pan travels between the user hatch and robot gate. The outer hatch closes before the inner gate opens. The tag reader checks identity at the dock.

04 / CONTROLS

The hardware behind the screen

Controller, input/output modules, safety relay, gateway, isolated power supply and backup power sit behind the removable operator fascia.

01 / IDENTIFY

The tag is the identity.

A permanent tag stays on the key. Staff select the exact address and unit; the loading drawer checks the tag before accepting a return. The address alone cannot identify a loose key.

02 / FILE

The cabinet does the walking.

A three-axis shuttle slides a captive tray from its slot and carries it to the loading drawer. Staff only touch the key. The tray and its reserved location remain inside the system.

03 / ACCOUNT

Know where every key went.

Each confirmed handoff records the employee, key, property, time, and location. Wrong tags and uncertain transfers stop the transaction rather than create a false “stored” record.

How the 1,000-key system fits together

Four modules, one directory

Each 250-position module has its own shuttle and loading drawer. The common search tells staff “use cabinet A, B, C, or D.” A single physical drawer for all 1,000 keys would need an additional transfer conveyor.

Four side by side5.6 m nominal width
Service / operating clearancesAdditional; to be designed

Rentvine supplies the address book

The proposed server reads properties and units, then stores the permanent property ID + unit ID alongside the key tag ID. Renaming an address does not change the key’s identity.

The local key database owns slots, custody and transactions. The cabinet controller owns motors, door interlocks and sensors. API credentials stay on the server.

Verified Rentvine API documentation ↗

Read-only property lookup was confirmed through the existing connection on 12 October 2026. This demonstration is offline and does not control hardware or update Rentvine.

What still needs a physical prototype

Engineering and commissioning

Validate tag reads next to metal keys, tray coupling, slot tolerances, motor sizing, braking, anti-fishing shutters, jam recovery and cycle life. Commission each key by physically checking it against its property before assigning its permanent tag.

Prototype one 24-slot section first. Use actual field keys and test successful returns, wrong tags, double deposits, missed pickups, jams and interrupted power.

Availability and failure behavior

Outer access door and inner robot shutter must never both unlock. Commit “stored” only after the tray and key are verified at their destination. A hardware safety circuit stops motion when access is open.

Power recovery checks the last slot, shuttle and dock before resuming. Network loss blocks new checkouts by default. A jam in one module leaves the other three available. Retrieval speed and reliability are unmeasured.
